person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating third person. The authorized publisher opening establishes third-person narration in the modern Cullinane frame, while numerous event quotes independently show external or omniscient narration in both contemporary and historical material. BookRags explicitly describes the entire novel as third person, and the structural sources confirm that the frame and historical reconstructions comprise the whole-book design. First-person forms in the quote set occur in dialogue, direct reflection, or gnomic language and are therefore local rather than autonomous narrative sections. The main limitation is that the Tier A excerpt covers only the opening, but the interior quote coverage and explicit whole-book POV description resolve that scope limitation; no credible alternating-person evidence emerged.
